name: comparator-offset-mc
description: Monte Carlo of the comparator preamplifier's input-referred offset over PVT, and of the code-correlated part of it: the change in offset over the +/-50 mV input-common-mode band single-ended mode produces. Includes a null control showing this PDK models no resistor local mismatch.
claim: README.md#target-specification -- Offset error <= 2 LSB untrimmed (3-sigma mismatch). This record measures the dominant term of the comparator's input-referred offset; spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S3 combines it with the latch term from sim/comparator-latch-offset-mc/ and compares the total against the 2 LSB bound.

sig_vos_mv.description: 1-sigma input-referred offset of the preamp. Its FLOOR is the guard against a mismatch-free population being recorded as a mismatch measurement: design.ngspice defaults sw_stat_mismatch = 0, so a deck that failed to turn mismatch on would report ~0 here (the companion positive result of sim/comparator-offset/'s symmetry null control). The process CEILING is the complementary assertion -- A_Vt lives in the fets_mm subckt and not in any corner section (devchar S3.3), so the dominant threshold term must be nearly corner-invariant; 15 % leaves room for the current-factor and V_ov-dependent terms that are NOT corner-invariant.

avt_back_mv_um.description: A_Vt back-extracted from the measured offset sigma: sigma(V_os) * sqrt(W_eff*L_eff) with W_eff = 40.1 um, L_eff = 0.85 um (devchar S3.3's effective-area rule, L_eff = L - 0.15, W_eff = W + 0.1). It must land at or ABOVE the 7.208 mV*um the standalone extraction measured, because the preamp's offset carries the input pair's threshold mismatch PLUS current-factor mismatch and the tail/load terms; a value BELOW 7.2 would mean the offset is being under-counted somewhere. The upper bound catches the opposite failure, an offset dominated by something other than the input pair.

sig_dvos_dn_uv.description: THE CODE-CORRELATED OFFSET TERM, low side: 1-sigma of V_os(V_cm - 50 mV) - V_os(V_cm) over the same draw. This is the quantity that decides whether offset cancellation is optional at all. Per prior-art-survey S3.1 a STATIC offset in a single-comparator SAR is a whole-converter offset, digitally removable; only the part that MOVES within a conversion is a linearity error. DR-0006 makes that part zero in differential mode (constant common mode) and residue/2-dependent in single-ended mode. 50 uV is 0.0155 LSB_se = 1/64 LSB, and the accuracy-critical late trials see ~5x less common-mode excursion than the +/-50 mV measured here -- so passing this bound is what licenses tier 0 (no cancellation + digital offset removal) in spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S4.

sig_dvos_up_uv.description: the same on the high side, V_os(V_cm + 50 mV) - V_os(V_cm).

av_sigma_pct.description: LOAD-BEARING SELF-CHECK, not a design number. The per-draw gain is taken as (op at +2 mV minus op at 0 mV) on the SAME instance, which is only valid if `alter` preserves the Monte Carlo draw between the two operating points. If it re-drew the mismatch instead, (d1-d0) would be dominated by the difference of two independent offsets -- each ~1.2 mV against a 2 mV probe -- and the extracted gain would scatter by tens of percent. A few percent here is the proof that the draw was preserved and hence that every V_os in this record is a real offset rather than a difference of two populations.

sig_rpair_uv.description: NULL CONTROL: 1-sigma resistance mismatch of two identical ppolyf_u_2k loads, read as 1 uA times their difference. It is EXPECTED TO BE ZERO. gf180mcu wires `*(1+mis_r*sw_stat_mismatch)` into every resistor subckt but hard-sets mis_r = 0 and leaves the area-scaled agauss expression commented out, so this PDK models no resistor local mismatch at all -- which means the offset sigma above contains NO load-mismatch contribution and that term must be budgeted by hand (spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S3.4). Keeping it as a check rather than a comment makes it a regression guard: a PDK revision that switches mis_r on fails here instead of silently changing every offset record in this repo.

mean_vos_uv.description: Population mean offset. It must be ~0 because the circuit is symmetric (sim/comparator-offset/ asserts that symmetry to 1 nV with mismatch off). The band is ~6 standard errors of the mean at N = 300 and sigma = 1.2 mV; a mean outside it would mean a systematic asymmetry is riding on top of the mismatch.

ptail_anchor_mv.description: CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR, same role as device-mismatch-mc's vgs_n_a_mv. The preamp tail-node voltage at the last Monte Carlo draw is a V_th proxy and is strongly corner- and temperature-dependent, unlike the mismatch sigma above, which is corner-invariant by construction. Without it this manifest has nothing that could fail under --sabotage-corners and its headline numbers would stay 'valid' with the corner runner stuck on typical.

vos_3sig_lsb.description: 3-sigma preamp offset in LSB_se (LSB_se = V_REF/1024 = 3.2227 mV, DR-0006). The ratified spec bounds TOTAL untrimmed offset at <= 2 LSB, and the StrongARM latch's contribution -- divided by the preamp gain -- has to fit alongside this term in quadrature. 1.75 LSB here leaves sqrt(2^2 - 1.75^2) = 0.97 LSB for the latch term, which is the headroom spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S3 spends.

evidence.mc_seed: ngspice `setseed 20260801` at the top of the control block, then 300 draws per PVT point via `reset` inside a dowhile loop (each reset re-evaluates the agauss expressions in the fets_mm subckts). The SAME seed is used at every PVT point -- common random numbers -- so movement of the reported sigma across the grid is a real PVT effect and not sampling noise; N for statistical-error purposes is 300, not 300 x 45. Seeding mechanism per sim/device-mismatch-mc/: `setseed <n>` is the only ngspice control that works here (`set rndseed` is silently ignored and `.options seed` freezes the draw).
evidence.mc_sigma: 1-sigma of the input-referred offset is reported directly, alongside the 3-sigma value the ratified <= 2 LSB offset row is stated at. Statistical precision on each sigma is 1/sqrt(2N) = 4.1 % at N = 300.
notes: TWO OPERATING POINTS PER DRAW, ONE INSTANCE. Gain is measured by `alter`-ing the shared differential source from 0 to +2 mV and re-running op on the SAME instance. Using two separate instances (as the deterministic deck next door does) would be wrong here: their mismatch draws are independent, so their difference would contain the offset difference rather than just the gain. av_sigma_pct is the check that this worked.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS RECORD. (a) The StrongARM latch's own offset -- it has no DC operating point, so it needs a transient and lives in sim/comparator-latch-offset-mc/; referred to the comparator input it is divided by the gain measured here. (b) Load-resistor mismatch, which this PDK does not model at all (see the sig_rpair_uv null control). (c) Current-factor (beta) mismatch is INCLUDED here -- unlike sim/device-mismatch-mc/, which biases in deep subthreshold specifically to suppress it -- because the preamp runs its pair in moderate inversion, which is exactly why avt_back_mv_um is expected to read above the 7.208 mV*um threshold-only coefficient.

sw_stat_mismatch is set in the NETLIST FRAGMENT, not in the manifest params: the harness emits manifest params ahead of the model includes and design.ngspice sets sw_stat_mismatch = 0, so a manifest param would be silently overridden and the whole Monte Carlo would collapse to sigma = 0.
